title: Emrys and the Orchard
premise: In the port city of Vellamare, Orsen Vasquez—raised in a pearl diver's tenement and indentured at nine to the Halloway Trading Company—has survived by being useful and unseen. When an infant is abandoned at the company warehouse with orders to 'forget the face,' Orsen secretly keeps the child, naming her Emrys after the drowned orchard their mother once described. As plague ships close the harbor and the company prepares to evacuate its favored families, Orsen must smuggle Emrys, their ailing father, and the sister they swore to protect toward one berth on the last ship—a berth that can hold only two. In the end, Orsen gives up their own place, sending Emrys and their sister to safety while staying behind in the burning orchard district, alive but unrecognizable to the company that owned them.
about_author: Zephyrine Nakamura is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing indenture ledgers from colonial trading ports. Their fiction excavates the small, unrecorded lives found in the margins of those documents.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Things
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. A day in the Halloway warehouse establishes Orsen's philosophy: carry little, want less, be invisible. They weigh cargo by hand and memorize faces they must never acknowledge. Emotional beat: quiet pride in survival that will be tested.

chapters.title: Salt in the Tenement
chapters.summary: Orsen visits their father, a pearl diver whose lungs are failing, and sister Marisol, who dreams of passage abroad. POV alternates briefly to Marisol's resentment of Orsen's company loyalty. Emotional beat: love strained by scarcity.

chapters.title: Instructions to Forget
chapters.summary: A clerk leaves an infant at the warehouse door with a sealed note: forget the face. Orsen, ordered to dispose of the bundle, instead hides her in the rope loft. Emotional beat: first crack in Orsen's invisibility.

chapters.title: Emrys
chapters.summary: Orsen names the child after the drowned orchard their mother described before the sea took her. Nightly feedings, stolen milk, near-discoveries. POV stays tight on Orsen's fear and tenderness. Emotional beat: dangerous attachment.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Debts
chapters.summary: Company auditor Mr. Quill audits Orsen's indenture, revealing years added through manufactured fines. Orsen realizes freedom was always arithmetic designed against them. Emotional beat: cold fury masked as deference.

chapters.title: Plague Flags
chapters.summary: A ship arrives flying the yellow flag; the harbor quarantines. Panic buying, rising prices, whispers of evacuation for company families only. Orsen sees the berth lists. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Marisol's Bargain
chapters.summary: Marisol discovers Emrys and, instead of betraying Orsen, offers to help—in exchange for a guaranteed place on the ship. POV shifts to Marisol. Emotional beat: alliance built on leverage, not trust.

chapters.title: Quill's Eye
chapters.summary: Quill grows suspicious of Orsen's errands and missing milk. He dangles promotion—and a berth—as bait for confession. Orsen lies fluently for the first time. Emotional beat: corruption begins its seduction.

chapters.title: The Orchard Beneath the Water
chapters.summary: Father, lucid with fever, tells the full story of the mother who dove for pearls beneath a submerged orchard and died refusing to sell her last pearl. Emotional beat: inheritance of defiance.

chapters.title: Berths for the Faithful
chapters.summary: The company posts its evacuation list: loyal clerks and favored bloodlines only. Orsen's name is absent; Marisol's is conditional. Emotional beat: the machinery of power made visible.

chapters.title: What Can Be Carried
chapters.summary: Orsen plans: forge a berth chit, bribe a dockhand, move Father to the warehouse. Each step costs something irreplaceable. Emotional beat: the price of survival itemized.

chapters.title: The Bribe That Bites
chapters.summary: The dockhand takes Orsen's savings and reports them to Quill anyway. Quill confronts Orsen privately—not with arrest, but an offer: inform on striking workers and earn three berths. Emotional beat: temptation wearing mercy's face.

chapters.title: Names on Paper
chapters.summary: Orsen considers it. Marisol argues survival justifies anything; Father, half-delirious, begs them not to become the company. POV braids all three voices. Emotional beat: family fracturing over ethics.

chapters.title: The Strike at Pier Nine
chapters.summary: Warehouse workers strike over quarantine conditions. Quill expects names. Orsen watches a striker's child go hungry and understands what betrayal purchases. Emotional beat: conscience catching fire.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Orsen burns the informant list instead of signing it, forfeiting all berths. Quill's mask drops—he reveals he knew about Emrys all along and has been waiting to see what Orsen would pay. Emotional beat: terror and liberation at once.

chapters.title: Flight Through the Rope Loft
chapters.summary: Quill moves to seize Emrys as leverage. Orsen smuggles the child out during a supply riot, Marisol covering their tracks. Emotional beat: desperate motion, no plan left but flight.

chapters.title: The Last Berth
chapters.summary: One berth remains on a chartered fishing boat leaving at dawn—room for two. Father's lungs are drowning him; Marisol refuses to leave without Orsen; Emrys cannot travel alone. The choice crystallizes. Emotional beat: unbearable arithmetic.

chapters.title: Which Family Member
chapters.summary: Climax. At the pier, Orsen puts Marisol and Emrys aboard—the sister who can raise the child, the child who carries the future. Father dies quietly on the quay holding Orsen's hand, freed from choosing. Emotional beat: grief fused with certainty.

chapters.title: The Burning Orchard District
chapters.summary: Quarantine fires consume the old quarter. Orsen, branded a thief by the company, vanishes into the smoke among strikers and the forgotten. Emotional beat: destruction as strange shelter.

chapters.title: Unrecognizable
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Quill scans refugee rolls and passes Orsen without a glance—the invisibility once a cage now armor. Orsen works the docks under another name. Emotional beat: survival redefined on one's own terms.

chapters.title: Letters Carried by Tide
chapters.summary: Smuggled letters arrive from Marisol: Emrys walks, laughs, asks about the orchard. Orsen sends back pressed flowers from the rebuilt hillside gardens. Emotional beat: love persisting across distance.

chapters.title: Emrys and the Orchard
chapters.summary: Years on, Orsen tends a real orchard above the harbor, paid in fruit and freedom. A young woman arrives with a child—Marisol and grown Emrys. The face Orsen was told to forget is the one that came home. Emotional beat: full-circle grace.
